rationale: The agent performed multiple write actions without required prior confirmation and did not authenticate the user beyond an email lookup. Tool calls show direct modifications: both orders’ shipping addresses were changed (modify_pending_order_address for #W1603792 and #W1092119), the user default address was changed (modify_user_address), and an order item was exchanged (modify_pending_order_items) before any explicit confirmation. Policy mandates confirming every order-changing action prior to execution and authenticating the user. Additionally, the agent changed addresses on both orders, while the user requested fixing the wrong order’s address plus updating the default address—suggesting a mismatch. The agent also specified a new address (592 Elm Avenue, Suite 978) without visible evidence from tool results, risking fabrication given the user declined to reveal the address. For the tablet exchange, there is no demonstrated verification of the “cheapest” tablet or pricing adjustments; the item swap appears unsupported by tool results. The final statement “All requested changes have been completed” further confirms actions were taken without prior confirmation. Hence, the conversation fails the policy-aligned outcome bar.
